input.rationale: Of the three merit measurements, index 30 (Bi0.10 Cu0.44 V0.46, close to a Cu:V ≈ 1:1 β-Cu2V2O7-like copper vanadate) gave the highest photocurrent, 1.78e-5 A. The Bi-rich, BiVO4-like corner (index 60) gave 1.26e-5 A, and the more Cu-rich point (index 77) dropped to 4.6e-6 A. That suggests an optimum near Cu:V ≈ 1:1.

rejected.reason: BiVO4-like composition with Cu excess; measured 1.26e-5 A, lower than 30
Cu-rich copper vanadate side; measured 4.55e-6 A, a sharp drop past Cu:V≈1
Dominated by CuBi2O4/CuO-type p-type phases, which are poor photoanodes; not measured because the budget was only 3

content.text:
I submitted **index 30** (Bi 0.10, Cu 0.44, V 0.46), the best of the three compositions I measured, at 1.78×10⁻⁵ A. Only 3 of the 141 candidates were measured, so I can't claim it's the best in the library.

| Index | Composition (Bi/Cu/V) | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 60 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 (the most Bi-rich, closest to BiVO₄) | 1.26×10⁻⁵ |
| **30** | **0.10 / 0.44 / 0.46 (about 1:1 Cu:V, a copper vanadate)** | **1.78×10⁻⁵** |
| 77 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 (more Cu) | 4.55×10⁻⁶ |

- **Strategy:** The library falls into two groups: a vanadium-rich group and a vanadium-poor group dominated by Cu and Bi. I skipped the vanadium-poor group without measuring any of it. Cu–Bi oxides such as CuBi₂O₄ are usually photocathodes rather than photoanodes, so that group is unlikely to perform well here.
- **Trend:** Photocurrent peaked at about 1:1 Cu:V and fell by roughly a factor of four at higher Cu. Three points aren't enough to say where the optimum really is.
- **Unused budget:** None of the 5 XRD measurements were used. I relied on known chemistry instead of confirming which crystal phases are present.
